kernel: Ancient Rome, the year of the four emperors. You're a freedwoman who runs a bathhouse where senators talk too freely, and every new emperor wants to know what you overheard under the last one. I want politics, survival, and family, and I want it to feel like real history, not a toga movie.

shape.note: through_lines is how many distinct story lines (each with its own ending) the shape preference suggests; the review decides whether each next one is worth building.

protagonist.who: You are a freedwoman who owns a working bathhouse in a Roman city district, where senators come to be scrubbed and speak too freely.
protagonist.history: You were freed by a senator's steward after years as a bathhouse attendant, and you bought the caldarium with a dowry and a debt to the imperial oil merchant.
protagonist.wants: to keep your daughter safe and the bathhouse open through the next succession without selling your memory for a price that breaks your family
protagonist.need: to find out whether the truth you kept can still be trusted to keep you alive
protagonist.can_do: scrub senators, overhear, keep a mental ledger, write names on a scroll, choose what to hand over, bargain with the Praetorian officer, and use the bathhouse's private steam room and service corridor
protagonist.cannot_do: make a new emperor accept less than a list, stop the Praetorian officer from arresting someone named, or keep your daughter from copying the list if she is in the chancery

ties.what: the man who has come to your bathhouse at each succession and offers a price for your silence
the owner of the bathhouse across the street who also listens and sells what he hears
the man who said the wrong thing in the caldarium and whose fate hangs on your memory
the scribe in the imperial chancery who copies the purge lists

protagonist.open: whether you become the honest keeper of the truth or the mother who buys safety with a name
protagonist.name: Flavia Crassa

arena.description: A Roman city district centered on a working bathhouse with caldarium, apodyterium, service corridor, and a small owner's house on the same street, plus the cold stone chamber of the new emperor's advisor in a nearby senator's villa.

pressure.description: Each emperor's death brings a new ruler's agents to the bathhouse within days, demanding the ledger of who spoke against the last man, while the purge lists your daughter copies begin to name senators from the caldarium.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked; the year of four emperors is told through the arrivals of agents, the sealing of the baths, and the growing purge list, because 3-0c licenses only soft detection_or_exposure

opposition.who_or_what: the Praetorian officer who collects testimony for each new emperor and runs the purge in the city district
opposition.wants: to be the man who found the real conspiracy and to buy his own safety with a price that makes your silence worth more than your daughter's life
opposition.means: he can arrest senators, seize the bathhouse, tax the oil and water, put your daughter's name on a purge list, and force the rival freedman's competing ledger into the new emperor's advisor's hands

events.what: The news of the old emperor's death reaches the caldarium; the steam stops, the senators freeze half-naked, and the Praetorian officer enters the apodyterium for the ledger.

A senator is dragged from the apodyterium by the Praetorian Guard, still dripping, while you watch from the service corridor; the rival freedman's ledger names a different senator, and the officer offers to spare your daughter if you confirm his list.

The new emperor's advisor summons you to a cold stone room with the scroll of names, and at home the family dinner goes quiet because your daughter has copied the purge list and the officer's seal is on the bathhouse door.

mediation.question: What do you hand to the new emperor: the honest testimony you kept, or the selective silence that keeps your family alive?

to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: write down what you actually heard in the caldarium and give the senator's name, even when the tired senator's fate depends on it
to_reach_pole_a.cost: the Praetorian officer can use the name to break the senator's household, and your daughter may be marked as the source of the list

to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: choose a name that protects your daughter, whether by naming the rival freedman, confirming the officer's list, or withholding the senator's name until the purge passes
to_reach_pole_b.cost: the truth you kept becomes a price, and the family may survive with the bathhouse sealed, the daughter's post lost, or the dignity broken

levers: the Praetorian officer's seal on the bathhouse door

turns.what_you_must_do: set the last name on the scroll before the advisor seals it

complications.description: The tired senator has been telling the Praetorian officer what he heard in the caldarium, because his household needs the officer's seal to keep his wife from the purge.
The daughter's copied purge list carries the officer's seal, so it is no longer a copy but the officer's own draft handed through her hand.

cast_seeds.wants: to identify the true conspirators to secure his own promotion and safety
cast_seeds.holds: the authority to arrest, the seal on the bathhouse door, and a list of names to confirm
cast_seeds.edge: he needs a real conspiracy to exist so his job matters, and he is willing to sacrifice the innocent to prove he found the truth
cast_seeds.tie: he has come to your bathhouse at each succession and offers a price for your silence
cast_seeds.voice: speaks in flat, procedural facts that carry the weight of a verdict: 'The water is cold. The list is short. Choose.'
cast_seeds.name: Aulus Domitius Rufus

cast_seeds.wants: to survive the purge by being forgotten
cast_seeds.holds: the specific, damning words he spoke in the caldarium that you overheard
cast_seeds.edge: he is so exhausted by the politics that he would rather be dead than wrong, yet he clings to life because he has nowhere else to go
cast_seeds.tie: he is the man who said the wrong thing in the caldarium and whose fate hangs on your memory
cast_seeds.voice: mumbles apologies to the steam and the stones, as if they are the only ones who can hear him: 'I was only thirsty. I was only thirsty when I said it.'
cast_seeds.name: Marcus Tullius Gallus

cast_seeds.wants: to own the district's secrets and sell them to the highest bidder
cast_seeds.holds: a competing ledger of names that contradicts yours
cast_seeds.edge: he listens as carefully as you do, but he trusts the coin more than the word, and he will sell your silence before he sells his own
cast_seeds.tie: he is the owner of the bathhouse across the street who also listens and sells what he hears
cast_seeds.voice: laughs too loudly to cover the fact that he is counting his profit: 'A name is just a price tag, isn't it? Let's see what it's worth.'
cast_seeds.name: Titus Marius Sulla

cast_seeds.wants: to keep her post in the chancery and stay out of the purge
cast_seeds.holds: the copy of the purge list she has already made in the imperial archive
cast_seeds.edge: she is competent and cold in her work, but she loves you enough to lie to you about what she has copied
cast_seeds.tie: she is the scribe in the imperial chancery who copies the purge lists and is your only family
cast_seeds.voice: uses the precise, dry language of the office to describe personal feelings: 'The ink is dry. The name is there. It cannot be unsaid.'
cast_seeds.breaking_point: turns against you if you make her choose between her career and your life without asking her first
cast_seeds.name: Tullia Paulla

cast_seeds.wants: to stabilize the new regime by identifying the ringleaders quickly
cast_seeds.holds: the final decision on which names are executed and which are spared
cast_seeds.edge: he is detached from the human cost, viewing the purge as a necessary surgery to save the body of the state
cast_seeds.tie: he holds the power that determines whether the officer's list or your testimony is accepted
cast_seeds.voice: speaks in calm, abstract terms about the health of the state: 'We do not need enemies. We need order. Order requires a few names.'
cast_seeds.name: Servius Aemilius Verus

framework.name: Fichtean curve
framework.shape: the story opens inside the first crisis and climbs through crises of different kinds to a climax, with almost no preamble and a short aftermath

modifier.name: In medias res
modifier.effect: Open inside the first premise turn's situation and fold the first beat's job into it; what the first beat would have shown arrives through what people do and say under pressure.

framework.reading: The story opens with the immediate threat of the first emperor's death and the arrival of the Praetorian officer, establishing a pattern of recurring crises that escalate with each succession. It builds through a series of high-stakes interrogations and betrayals, where the cost of survival rises from political favor to family safety, landing on a final confrontation where the protagonist must choose between honest testimony and the selective silence required to keep her daughter alive.
framework.why: Its shape opens inside the first crisis (the officer's arrival in Turn 1) and climbs through distinct crises of different kinds (the trade in Turn 2, the rescue/family threat in Turn 3) to a climax, which matches the escalating trajectory in 3b.primary_trajectory and the recurring instances in 3-0a.decision_mechanism. Unlike three_act, which requires a distinct setup before the inciting incident, or seven_point, which relies on a midpoint shift in agency, fichtean_curve's continuous crisis-driven structure better fits the 'year of the four emperors' premise where the threat is constant and the stakes escalate without a lull.

beats.name: Opening crisis
beats.job: the story opens inside the first crisis; who the protagonist is and what is at stake are shown by how it is met

beats.name: Second crisis
beats.job: a worse crisis, different in kind; what the first one spent or revealed shapes it

beats.name: Third crisis
beats.job: the price of the earlier ways through comes due, and the opposition makes its strongest move

beats.name: Climax
beats.job: the last crisis, where the story's question is answered by what the protagonist does

beats.name: Aftermath
beats.job: brief: what is left, and what it cost

T1.title: The Ledger of the Caldarium
T1.motivation: Flavia Crassa begins wanting only to keep the bathhouse open and Tullia Paulla safe through the next succession, but the pressure of the ledger turns her want into the need to know whether the truth she has kept can still be trusted to keep them alive.
T1.strategy: She answers each demand for names with the smallest name that will hold the officer back, using the bathhouse ledger, the rival freedman's competing list, and the service corridor to keep the caldarium's testimony from being taken whole.
T1.turning_point: When Tullia Paulla hands the copied purge list at the door of the cold stone room and names Marcus Tullius Gallus first, the truth is no longer something Flavia can keep in her own hand; the senator's fate and her daughter's post are now bound to the same scroll.

ending.title: The Name in the Ink
ending.summary: The new emperor receives the honest testimony of the caldarium, with Marcus Tullius Gallus's name written in Flavia Crassa's hand, and the price is the senator's household broken and Tullia Paulla marked as the source of the list. The bathhouse keeps its door under the officer's seal, but the family survives only with the truth now standing between them and the next purge.
ending.changed: the caldarium's testimony is on the emperor's scroll, the officer's seal is on the bathhouse door, and Tullia Paulla's name is written as the source of the list

T2.title: The Rival's Ledger
T2.motivation: Flavia Crassa begins wanting to keep Tullia Paulla safe without her own hand becoming the emperor's source, and after the officer tears the bathhouse scroll and reads the rival's name aloud, she comes to want the family's safety to come from Titus Marius Sulla's ledger instead of the caldarium's testimony; by the end she wants only the bathhouse to remain open and Tullia unmarked, even if the truth of the steam room is left unasked.
T2.strategy: Let the rival freedman's ledger do the work: give the officer a reason to take the rival's list, keep the bathhouse running under the rival's oil contract, and make sure Tullia Paulla's name is not written as the source of the purge.
T2.turning_point: The torn scroll. Once Aulus Domitius Rufus tears the bathhouse ledger and reads Titus Marius Sulla's name aloud, Flavia Crassa's own testimony is no longer the thing that saves her family; the rival's competing list becomes the price of their safety.
T2.differs_from: T1 answers with honest testimony: Flavia Crassa gives Marcus Tullius Gallus's name, Tullia Paulla is marked as the source, and the caldarium's memory becomes the emperor's evidence; this line answers with family survival: the rival freedman's list becomes the emperor's source, Tullia Paulla is not marked, and the different senator's household is broken instead.

ending.title: The Rival's Ledger
ending.summary: The new emperor receives the rival freedman's list instead of the caldarium's testimony, and Tullia Paulla's name is not marked as the source. The bathhouse stays open under the rival's oil contract, but the different senator's household is broken and the caldarium's own memory is left unasked.
ending.changed: the rival's ledger is the emperor's source, and the bathhouse survives under his contract

divergence.trigger: you let the officer tear your scroll and read the rival's name aloud
divergence.instead_of: you gave the officer the bathhouse ledger scroll with Marcus Tullius Gallus's name in your own hand
divergence.opportunity: Add to N02 that Titus Marius Sulla has the service corridor key for the night and has already told Aulus Domitius Rufus that you were listening in the caldarium, so the officer expects a competing ledger rather than only the bathhouse scroll.
divergence.shift: The officer tears your scroll and reads the rival's name aloud, so your own hand is no longer the source he needs; he offers to spare Tullia Paulla if the rival's list stands, and the oil contract becomes the price of keeping the bathhouse open.

T2.why: The seed works as a line because it changes the source of testimony: the caldarium's memory is replaced by the rival freedman's ledger, so the family survives without Tullia Paulla being marked as the source. The seed's reference to the rival having heard the stopped steam is folded into N02 as an added pressure rather than a change to the shared N01.

T3.title: The Blank Bottom
T3.motivation: Flavia Crassa begins wanting to keep Tullia Paulla safe without her own hand becoming the emperor's source again, and after the copied list and the seal on the bathhouse door she comes to want Servius Aemilius Verus to choose rather than be forced, because her hand has already been marked as the source; by the end she wants only the family to survive under the officer's list with the caldarium's testimony unspoken.
T3.strategy: Keep the caldarium's testimony in her own hand, bring the copied list to the cold stone room, and leave the bottom of the scroll blank so the advisor must choose between her memory and Aulus Domitius Rufus's list.
T3.turning_point: The blank bottom of the scroll in the cold stone room: once Flavia Crassa leaves it blank, the choice and the cost pass from her hand to the advisor's seal and the officer's list.
T3.differs_from: It differs from T1 in that T1 hands the caldarium's honest testimony to the emperor and leaves the bathhouse open under the officer's seal, while this line withholds the senator's name and leaves the bathhouse sealed under the officer's list, so the family survives in silence rather than by testimony. It differs from T2 in that T2 lets the rival freedman's ledger become the price and keeps the bathhouse open under the rival's oil contract, while this line refuses to make either the caldarium or the rival the source and lets the officer's list seal the door, leaving the truth unasked under a closed bathhouse.

ending.title: The Blank Bottom
ending.summary: Servius Aemilius Verus chooses Aulus Domitius Rufus's list and seals the bathhouse, so the caldarium's testimony is never handed over as a name. Tullia Paulla remains with you, but the door is closed and the truth you kept becomes a silence the family must live under.
ending.changed: the bathhouse is sealed and the emperor's list is the officer's, not the caldarium's

divergence.trigger: you gave Servius Aemilius Verus your own hand and left the bottom of the scroll blank
divergence.instead_of: you wrote Marcus Tullius Gallus at the bottom of the scroll in Servius Aemilius Verus's presence and gave him the caldarium's testimony
divergence.shift: You see that Aulus Domitius Rufus's list is already in the room and that your own hand is marked as the source, so writing Marcus Tullius Gallus would make Tullia Paulla pay for the caldarium's testimony a second time; you want the advisor to take the choice and the cost.

T3.why: The seed holds as given: turn 4's way 3 is still unused, and leaving the scroll blank changes the answer from T1's honest testimony and T2's rival-ledger price to a world where the caldarium's testimony is withheld and the bathhouse is sealed under the officer's list.

N01.adapted: The news of the old emperor's death reaches the caldarium, the steam stops, and the senators freeze half-naked while Aulus Domitius Rufus enters the apodyterium and presses his seal onto a wax tablet in Flavia Crassa's hand. The first name on the tablet is Marcus Tullius Gallus, and every man in the apodyterium hears his own name called out of the bathhouse ledger.
N01.title: The First Name
N01.summary: The news of the old emperor's death reaches the caldarium, and the steam stops as the senators freeze half-naked. You make Aulus Domitius Rufus press his seal onto a wax tablet in your hand, and the first name he expects is Marcus Tullius Gallus. Every man in the apodyterium hears the name called out of the bathhouse ledger, and Titus Marius Sulla stands by the door counting what it is worth.
N01.image: the sealed wax tablet, the first name wet in the steam

N02.adapted: Marcus Tullius Gallus is dragged from the apodyterium by the Praetorian Guard, still dripping, while Flavia Crassa watches from the service corridor and Titus Marius Sulla's ledger names a different senator. Aulus Domitius Rufus offers to spare Tullia Paulla if Flavia confirms his list, and she gives him the bathhouse ledger scroll with Marcus Tullius Gallus's name in her own hand, so the senator is taken to the guard's cell and Tullia Paulla's name is written on the scroll as the source.
N02.title: The Scroll as Source
N02.summary: Marcus Tullius Gallus is dragged from the apodyterium by the Praetorian Guard, still dripping, while you watch from the service corridor. Titus Marius Sulla's ledger names a different senator, but Aulus Domitius Rufus offers to spare Tullia Paulla if you confirm his list. You give him the bathhouse ledger scroll with Gallus's name in your own hand, so the senator is taken to the guard's cell and Tullia Paulla's name is written on the scroll as the source.
N02.image: the ledger scroll with Tullia Paulla's name written as the source

additions.text: Add to N02 that Titus Marius Sulla has the service corridor key for the night and has already told Aulus Domitius Rufus that you were listening in the caldarium, so the officer expects a competing ledger rather than only the bathhouse scroll.

N03.adapted: At home the family dinner goes quiet because Tullia Paulla has copied the purge list and Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal is on the bathhouse door. Flavia Crassa asks Tullia Paulla what her hand will do before Servius Aemilius Verus sees the copied list, and Tullia Paulla hands the scroll to her at the door of the cold stone room, naming Marcus Tullius Gallus first so the advisor hears the name and the daughter's chancery post is spent as the price of the list coming back.
N03.title: The Copied List
N03.summary: At home the family dinner goes quiet because Tullia Paulla has copied the purge list and Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal is on the bathhouse door. You ask Tullia what her hand will do before Servius Aemilius Verus sees the copied list, and she hands the scroll to you at the door of the cold stone room. She names Marcus Tullius Gallus first, so the advisor hears the name and her chancery post is spent as the price of the list coming back.
N03.image: the copied purge list held at the door of the cold stone room

N04.adapted: In the cold stone room Flavia Crassa writes Marcus Tullius Gallus at the bottom of the scroll in Servius Aemilius Verus's presence and gives him the caldarium's testimony. Aulus Domitius Rufus seals the scroll and breaks the senator's household, and Tullia Paulla's hand remains marked as the source of the list.
N04.title: The Last Name
N04.summary: Servius Aemilius Verus holds the scroll open in the cold stone room while Titus Marius Sulla presses his competing ledger against the table, and you write Marcus Tullius Gallus at the bottom and give the advisor the caldarium's testimony. Aulus Domitius Rufus seals the scroll before the tired senator can answer, and his men go out to break the senator's household. Tullia Paulla's hand remains marked as the source of the list.
N04.image: the seal pressed across Gallus's wet ink

N05.adapted: The bathhouse reopens under Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal, and Flavia Crassa scrubs the caldarium stones with Tullia Paulla's name still on the emperor's scroll. Marcus Tullius Gallus is gone from the district, and the truth Flavia Crassa kept is now a price the next emperor will know to ask.
N05.title: The Reopened Door
N05.summary: The bathhouse reopens under Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal, and you scrub the caldarium stones while Tullia Paulla's name stays on the emperor's scroll. Marcus Tullius Gallus is gone from the district, and the new emperor now holds the honest testimony of the caldarium with his name written in your hand. The family survives only with that truth standing between you and the next purge.
N05.image: the sealed door over the wet caldarium stones

T2N01.adapted: At home the family dinner goes quiet because Tullia Paulla has copied the purge list and Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal is on the bathhouse door. Flavia Crassa sends Marcus Tullius Gallus's steward to the chancery with a bathhouse oil jar and asks for the scroll in the oil, and Tullia Paulla slips the copied list into the jar; her hand is burned by the wax, but her name is not written as the source.
T2N01.title: The Wax-Sealed Jar
T2N01.summary: The summons to the cold stone room arrives with Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal already pressed on the bathhouse door, and the family dinner in the owner's dining room goes quiet as Tullia Paulla sets down the purge list she copied in the chancery. You send the tired senator's steward to the chancery with a bathhouse oil jar and ask for the scroll sealed in the wax, and Tullia Paulla slips the copied list into the jar before the lid is shut. Her hand is burned by the hot wax, but her name is not written as the source of the purge.
T2N01.image: a clay oil jar with a cracked wax seal, the copied list visible through the gap in the lid

T2N02.adapted: In the cold stone room Flavia Crassa hands Servius Aemilius Verus the rival freedman's list and Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal, and the scroll names Titus Marius Sulla. The advisor seals the rival's ledger as the emperor's source, the different senator's household is broken, and the bathhouse keeps its door under the rival's oil contract.
T2N02.title: The Rival's Name
T2N02.summary: You stand in the cold stone room with the rival freedman's list in your hand and Aulus Domitius Rufus's seal pressed into the wax, and Servius Aemilius Verus reads Titus Marius Sulla's name from the scroll before sealing the rival's ledger as the emperor's source. Tullia Paulla stands at the wall and hears her post in the chancery struck from the roll, and Titus Marius Sulla is taken from the room by the Praetorian officer while the bathhouse door is marked open under the rival's oil contract.
T2N02.image: the advisor's seal pressed into fresh wax on a rival's ledger, the name Titus Marius Sulla visible beneath the thumbprint

T2N03.adapted: The bathhouse reopens with the rival's oil contract on the door and Tullia Paulla's name unmarked on the emperor's scroll. The caldarium's own testimony is left unasked, and the family survives because the rival's ledger, not the bathhouse ledger, became the price of their safety.
T2N03.title: The Door Stays Open
T2N03.summary: The bathhouse reopens with the rival's oil contract nailed to the apodyterium door and Tullia Paulla's name unmarked on the emperor's scroll. The caldarium steams as it always has, and no one asks the steam room what it heard; the family survives because the rival's ledger, not the bathhouse testimony, became the price of their safety.
T2N03.image: the rival's oil contract nailed to the bathhouse door, the caldarium's steam rising past it unasked

T3N01.adapted: Aulus Domitius Rufus seals the bathhouse door with the officer's list and leaves Tullia Paulla inside, not in the guard's cell, because you do not ask her to copy the list again; the caldarium stones go cold and the scroll of names stands as the emperor's order, not the caldarium's testimony.
T3N01.title: The Sealed Door
T3N01.summary: Servius Aemilius Verus chooses Aulus Domitius Rufus's list in the cold stone room and sends Aulus to seal the apodyterium door, while the blank bottom of your own hand stays unmarked. Aulus seals the door with the officer's list and leaves Tullia Paulla inside rather than in the guard's cell, since you do not ask her to copy the list again. The caldarium stones go cold, and the scroll of names stands as the emperor's order while the family lives under the sealed door in silence.
T3N01.image: the blank bottom of the scroll under the officer's seal

promises.reading: This is a historical thriller set in the turbulent Year of the Four Emperors (69 CE), where the player is a freedwoman whose bathhouse serves as the Senate's confessional. The writer wants the grit of real Roman politics—the smell of sweat and blood, the weight of a name spoken in the wrong ear—rather than a mythic spectacle. They are hoping to feel the sharp, cold thrill of survival: knowing that one slip of the tongue can save a daughter or doom a friend.
promises.player_fantasy: To be the keeper of secrets in a city that is eating itself, where your value is your silence and your danger is your memory.

promises.what: the steam room as a confessional: senators stripping away their rank along with their tunics, speaking truths they would never voice in the Forum, while the player scrubs their backs
promises.why: this is the unique vantage point; the bathhouse is where the power structure becomes intimate and vulnerable

promises.what: the succession shock: the moment the old emperor dies or is declared dead, and the new ruler's agents arrive to demand the 'ledger' of who said what
promises.why: this is the inciting incident and the recurring engine; the player must decide who to protect and who to sacrifice

promises.what: the family stake: a specific relative (daughter, son, or brother) who is in the path of the new emperor's purge, making the player's testimony a life-or-death currency
promises.why: the 'family' element in the Kernel needs a face; without it, the politics are abstract

promises.what: the texture of the 'real': the specific, gritty details of Roman life—the price of oil, the quality of the water, the political slang of the streets—grounding the high stakes in daily reality
promises.why: the Kernel explicitly rejects the 'toga movie'; the audience expects the weight of history, not just the drama

promises.what: the rival freedman or rival bathhouse owner who has been listening too, creating a competition for the truth that is as dangerous as the emperor himself
promises.why: the player cannot be the only source; the web of spies needs a competitor to make the testimony valuable

set_pieces.scene: the moment the news of the emperor's death reaches the bathhouse: the water stops, the senators freeze, and the silence is louder than the screaming outside
a senator being dragged out of the baths by the Praetorian Guard, still half-naked and dripping, while the player watches from the service corridor, deciding whether to speak
the player standing before the new emperor's advisor in a cold, stone room, holding a scroll of names, feeling the weight of every life in the ink
set_pieces.where: a private chamber in the Palatine or a senator's villa

set_pieces.scene: the family dinner that is not a dinner: the player's family eating in silence, knowing that the next meal might be their last, or the last time they are free
set_pieces.where: the player's modest home near the baths

promises.tone_engine: Grounded and serious: the tone is produced by the physicality of the bathhouse (the heat, the water, the labor) contrasting with the cold, distant politics. Wary vigilance: the player is always listening, always calculating, and the reader feels the tension of a secret kept too long.
obligatory_cast: a Praetorian officer who is looking for a scapegoat and is willing to buy silence with a price that is too high
a senator who is not a villain, but a man who said the wrong thing because he was tired, and whose fate hangs on the player's memory
must_not: no mythological elements: no gods intervening, no omens that are more than coincidence, no magical properties to the water
no 'toga movie' spectacle: no chariot races, no colosseum fights, no grand public speeches unless they are overheard in the bathhouse
